status: Synthetic developer-authored inputs, observations and costs; no physical product or waste was measured.
initial_prompt: I want to make a desk cable organizer from recovered plastic and cork, but the cork content in my incoming mix changes. How can I decide what to try while keeping my deflection and thickness targets and considering cost?

case.product_and_use: A non-load-bearing indoor desk cable organizer tray, with the same fictional 200 by 80 mm nominal footprint for each setup.
case.materials_and_variation: Each whole recipe contains only recovered HDPE matrix and cork filler; the HDPE is the matrix/binder, with no additional binder. Quantities, cork percentages and prices all use the same as-received mass basis. The incoming characterized portion contains an unknown 28–32 mass percent cork. The separately characterized added stock contains 5 mass percent cork, with the remainder HDPE.
case.process_and_equipment: The same fictional compression-molding process P and nominal footprint are stated for both recorded setups, with process settings unspecified. Home planning only: no physical handling, processing, measuring equipment or lab access is available during this exercise.

costs.scope: Materials only. Energy, direct labor and all other costs are explicitly excluded.

calculator.units: kg, mass percent, EUR per planned usable item
calculator.addition_formula: For a known input fraction p, exact point t and added-stock fraction s, x = m * (p - t) / (t - s), provided t differs from s. The same x must satisfy both input endpoints for a fixed-addition range.
calculator.cost_formula: sum(entered component kg × price EUR/kg) / planned usable items; excluded costs remain excluded
